checks: Verified source 30917746e40e143c §§1–3 (1), and §4 on the ordinary orientations and uniform comparison. The draft proves the example for the stated class of symmetric concave profiles and gives a direct strict-uniqueness argument using one orbit direction.

The lattice support has exactly the three displayed vertices and their mean zero, and the real product makes all four sampled fibers equal to K. The within-fiber covariance is positive definite. An affine barycentric permutation preserves uniform volume and hence its centered linear part A satisfies AΣAᵀ=Σ. Thus u↦Aᵀu preserves Γ(u). The three cyclic centered actions sum to zero, so an invariant gradient is zero, and the orbit of any normalized nonzero covector has exactly three elements with zero sum.

Concavity and cyclic invariance put the maximum of f at g. If another x attained it, the segment from g to x would be constant at the maximum. Its nontrivial interior subsegment contradicts strict own-interior concavity, including when x is on the boundary.

At g the area on which the ramp and ordinary cap can differ lies in the displayed band, whose area is at most its physical width times the diameter of K. The normalized covector ellipse is compact and bounded away from zero, so convergence is uniform. The ordinary cap mass is continuous there because the boundary line has area zero.

For a one-vertex cap through g, the intercepted side coordinates give α^(-1)+β^(-1)=3 and α,β≤1. The reciprocal product lies between 2 and 9/4, proving the area range and the unique minimum at α=β=2/3. The two-vertex orientation is complementary and at least 1/2; through-vertex cases occur at the endpoints. This proves q_(ε,h)→4V/9 and localization of every minimizing direction to the three ordinary orientations by compactness.

For each x≠g, some minimizing orbit direction at g has u·(x−g)≥0 by zero sum. Its offset change at x is strictly negative. A uniform inball at g ensures that at small ε,h the own strip has positive area, and the derivative of integrated capture with respect to the normalized offset is area of the strip divided by h. Local strict positivity and global monotonicity therefore imply a strict decrease for any negative offset. Testing this one direction gives θ_(ε,h)(x)<q_(ε,h).

For any center oblique normal, the cyclic coupling of three uniform outer points has sums Σ_j(X_j−g)=0 and Σ_jv_j=0. The total outer margin is positive, giving at least one saturated ramp at each sample and outer capture ≥V. Each listed base tilt has matched score 2 and other scores −1, so a large finite multiplier attains that lower bound while leaving the own term unchanged. Pure-base caps through zero have mass ≥2V. These cover all normal types.

At an outer base a finite exposing tilt isolates the own minimizing cap. At any middle mark a matched saturation tilt gives the upper bound V+θ_(ε,h)(x). These bounds and strict own uniqueness give the claimed global singleton. In the selected menu only the center strip contributes to the threshold derivative, so each strip's base centroid is zero. Cyclic covariance invariance and volume preservation make the three derivatives equal and positive, giving both balance and response weights 1/3.
